Elliot — thanks for the note and congrats on the cohort. Short answer: we can usually make credits work toward a Dedicated pilot but there are a couple of constraints (billing/recognition and legal/terms). I copied Marissa from GTM to propose an ops path.

High level options we commonly offer:
- Apply credits as a one-time invoice credit against the first Dedicated invoice (limited to credit amount and must be documented in an addendum).
- Convert credits into a prepaid invoice line (treated as deferred revenue on our side; requires a simple addendum).
- If you need ongoing discounted committed pricing, we can propose a short-term discount + carveout.

Can you confirm expected spend profile (estimated monthly token/throughput spend) and whether you need the credits to fully cover the pilot or just offset the activation month?

If you can, include procurement/contact for contracting; Marissa will follow up on commercial mechanics.

—Rishi
Head of Sales Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hey Elliot — quick follow-up from commercial. Thanks for attaching the award. We dug into the program terms and attached a short "mechanics" workbook that shows a couple of ways to structure this. TL;DR: we can either

1) Apply up to the credit amount as a one-time credit against the first Dedicated invoice (no change to baseline contract language; we document in an addendum that the credit is applied to invoice X).

2) Convert the cohort credit into a prepaid line on your invoice (Redwood books as deferred revenue and you get credit balance to draw against over the pilot). This requires a 1-page addendum and sign-off from finance.

3) If you'd prefer committed pricing, we can do a 3-month reserved commitment with a pilot discount (we're suggesting 20% off list for the first 3 months) in exchange for a short-term commitment. That path usually needs procurement + legal.

I've looped in Lauren from Finance/Legal to confirm the accounting/tax steps — Lauren, any red flags on option 2 or on applying credits to a Dedicated invoice?

Attached: proposed_mop.xlsx — row 1 shows a sample conversion that would fully cover month 1 using the cohort balance.

If that all sounds fine, we can draft the addendum and route via DocuSign.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi all — from Finance/Legal perspective: option 2 (convert credits to a prepaid invoice line) is the cleanest path operationally because it preserves how we recognize revenue and avoids reclassifying cohort awards. Two items to flag:

- We will need a short addendum that lists the credit amount, the invoice(s) it can be applied against (or that it becomes a prepayment pool), and the drawdown schedule (we recommend 90 days).
- Tax/accounting: the cohort credit will be reflected as a contra on your invoice; depending on Aster's jurisdiction you'll want to run this by your tax advisor. We can provide a summary of how we treat credits (see attached redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf for compliance context and a short note on revenue recognition).

If you decide on the committed-pricing path (option 3), Procurement will need an SOW/addendum plus the typical PO or signature; that delays start by ~3–5 business days depending on your legal.

I attached a draft conversion SOW/one-pager that we can update with dollar amounts and term. If everyone is aligned I can push the addendum to DocuSign by EOD.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Finance Contracts
Redwood Inference
